subject: Jacqueline Torres Roth City Council Candidacy
overview: City Council candidate Jacqueline Torres-Roth outlined her platform focusing on environmental sustainability, transit accessibility, and equitable housing. The discussion highlighted her goals for increasing diversity in city government and reforming the process for board and commission appointments.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Local Background
items.summary: Jacqueline Torres-Roth introduced her background as a member of the Solid Waste Task Force, the Arts Council, and the Pride Planning Committee.

items.title: Path to Local Politics
items.summary: The candidate described her journey from a childhood interest in voting and an internship with Senator Markey to active community organizing in Medford.

items.title: Environmental and Sustainability Priorities
items.summary: Torres-Roth detailed a platform for a "thriving environment," advocating for increased tree canopy, cooling stations, and expanded composting initiatives.

items.title: Public Transportation and Infrastructure
items.summary: The candidate called for investment in the Orange Line and commuter rail while highlighting the need for more frequent and accessible bus routes between transit hubs.

items.title: Affordable Housing and Zoning Reform
items.summary: Torres-Roth emphasized reaching the state's 10% affordable housing requirement through equitable zoning reform and mixed-use development in Medford and Haines Squares.

items.title: Equity and Representation in Governance
items.summary: The candidate proposed diversifying city leadership by intentionally appointing Black, Brown, and LGBTQ+ residents to boards and commissions.

items.title: Accessibility of Boards and Commissions
items.summary: Torres-Roth critiqued the current appointment process for its lack of transparency and advocated for reducing barriers such as meeting times and digital access.

items.title: Community Culture and Quality of Life
items.summary: The candidate discussed the importance of arts programming and shared her goal to improve Medford's walkability score to compete with neighboring cities.

items.title: Upcoming Community Events
items.summary: Torres-Roth highlighted several upcoming local events, including the Pride flag raising, the city's first PorchFest, and Community Day.
